stem:
The diagram shows Bilal’s known bar magnet with its South pole facing unmarked bar Y. The facing ends push apart.

What does this tell him about bar Y?

options.text: Bar Y is a magnet; only a magnet can repel another magnet.
Bar Y is ordinary iron; attraction alone would already prove it is a magnet.
Bar Y is a magnet because both bars are drawn the same length.
Bar Y is a magnet only if a North pole attracts it, not if the ends push apart.

teacher.key_rationale: Repulsion identifies a magnet. Attraction alone cannot, because plain iron is also attracted. Same drawn length is not evidence. Attraction is not the test that settles the question.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source force diagram into known magnet (S facing) and unmarked bar Y with repulsion arrows.
